# Turn an Alexa+ List into a Family Message Board Anyone at Home Can Use

> **In short:** Create a custom list in the Alexa app — call it *Family Board* — and everyone at home can add a note by saying "Alexa, add … to Family Board" to your Echo. You read the board in the Alexa app, on an Echo with a screen, or with Alexa+ in your web browser. Setup takes about five minutes.

You probably already ask Alexa to add milk to the shopping list. This guide uses the same idea for the small messages a family passes around all day: "the plumber comes at 10", "Sam needs a ride after practice", "we're out of printer paper". Instead of a fridge note nobody sees, the note goes on one list that lives on your Amazon account.

## Before you start
- **At least one Echo device** set up with your Amazon account, in a spot the family uses — a kitchen counter works well. Everyone who talks to that Echo can add notes to your board.
- **The Alexa app** on your phone, signed in with the same Amazon account.
- **Optional: Alexa+.** With Alexa+, you can also manage your lists in a web browser at alexa.com. Amazon says that browser version is available only with Alexa+.
- **Time needed:** about 5 minutes to set up, then a few seconds per note.

## Step 1 — Create the board as a custom list
Open the **Alexa app**, tap **More**, then tap **Lists & Notes**. Tap **Create List**, type a short name that is easy to say out loud, then tap **Done**. This guide uses *Family Board*.

**If it looks different:** you can also start by voice — Amazon's list help uses "Alexa, create a list" as an example. If you have Alexa+ in your browser, go to alexa.com, select **Lists** in the left navigation, then select **Add Custom List**, type the name and confirm with **OK**.

**You'll know it worked when** *Family Board* appears among your lists under **Lists & Notes**.

## Step 2 — Post the first note by voice
Stand near your Echo and add a note with the list's name at the end. Amazon's pattern for this is "Add [item] to [list name]" — say the whole note as the item.

💬 Example: say *"Alexa, add pick up the dry cleaning to Family Board."*

**If it looks different:** you can also type a note: open *Family Board* in the Alexa app and tap **Add Item**.

**You'll know it worked when** the note shows up when you open *Family Board* in the Alexa app.

## Step 3 — Let everyone else post the same way
Show the family the one sentence they need. Anyone at home can walk up to your Echo and use it — they don't need the app or their own account, because the Echo adds the note to the list on your account.

💬 Example: your partner says *"Alexa, add Sam has soccer practice at four to Family Board."*

**If it looks different:** if a note doesn't appear, open the app and check your other lists — when Alexa doesn't catch the list name, the note can end up on another list, such as your shopping list.

**You'll know it worked when** a note spoken by someone else appears on *Family Board* in your app.

## Step 4 — Read the board
Pick the way that fits the moment:
- **In the Alexa app:** tap **More**, then **Lists & Notes**, then *Family Board*.
- **On an Echo with a screen:** say *"Alexa, show me my Family Board."* Amazon lists "Show me my [list name]" for Echo devices with a screen.
- **Out loud:** Amazon's example for hearing a list is "Alexa, what's on my shopping list?" — ask the same way with your board's name, such as *"Alexa, what's on my Family Board?"* If Alexa doesn't read it, use the app instead.
- **In a browser with Alexa+:** at alexa.com, select **Lists** in the left navigation to open your lists in a side panel.

**You'll know it worked when** you can see or hear the notes without anyone having to repeat them.

## Step 5 — Clear old notes
A board only works if it stays short. When something is done, remove it by voice — Amazon's pattern is "Remove [item] from my [list name]" — or tap it in the app. To start fresh, Amazon's example is "Clear my [list name]."

💬 Example: *"Alexa, remove pick up the dry cleaning from my Family Board."* or *"Alexa, clear my Family Board."*

**If it looks different:** with Alexa+ in your browser, you can select an item's check box when it's done, or select **Delete** to remove it completely.

**You'll know it worked when** only the notes that still matter are left on the board.

## Common mistakes
- **Forgetting the list name.** If you say "Alexa, add a dentist appointment" without "to Family Board", the note may land on a different list.
  - **Fix:** always end the sentence with the board's name, and pick a name that is short and easy to say.
- **Expecting the board in someone else's app.** The board belongs to the Amazon account your Echo uses. Amazon's help names the Amazon Shopping List as the list adults in an Amazon Family share — it doesn't say custom lists are shared.
  - **Fix:** use the board through the Echo, or check it in the Alexa app signed in to your account.
- **Putting private things on the board.** Anyone near the Echo can ask to hear or see it.
  - **Fix:** keep the board for household logistics, and keep private notes off it.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** fewer "did you tell me about…?" moments. Adding a note takes one sentence, and nobody has to remember to open an app to leave it.
- **For your business or work:** the same trick works for a home office — a second list called *Work Notes* catches ideas you think of while cooking or cleaning.
- **If you want to go further:** try a second, short list for things that matter today, such as *Errands Today*, and clear it every evening. Two short lists are easier to scan than one long one.

## Try it now
Open the Alexa app, tap **More → Lists & Notes → Create List**, and name it *Family Board*. Then walk to your Echo and say: *"Alexa, add [your note] to Family Board."* Tonight, show the family that one sentence — the board is ready.
